name: iPhone Duo
criticsTake: Critics say Apple's first foldable is the best-built foldable yet. The titanium hinge and the matte nano-texture display that hides the crease draw wide praise, and PCMag calls its battery life class-leading. It is also heavy at 254 g and starts at $1,999, it has no Face ID or telephoto camera, and many apps are not optimized yet, so The Verge, Wired and CNN suggest waiting.

gripes: Heavy at 254 g

name: iPhone 18 Pro
criticsTake: Critics call the iPhone 18 Pro an excellent but iterative upgrade. The A20 Pro chip, longer battery life and a variable-aperture main camera with manual controls earn near-universal praise, while the unchanged design, extra weight and $100 price increase leave most reviewers telling iPhone 17 Pro owners to wait.

name: Galaxy Z Fold 8
criticsTake: Critics love the Galaxy Z Fold 8's new wider, passport-shaped design, which makes it easy to use shut and great for video and games when open. Bright displays with a barely visible crease and solid battery life round out the praise. Nearly every review knocks the missing telephoto camera, and many flag the price, the IP48 rating and apps that don't yet fit the new screen shape.

Strong performance and all-day battery

name: iPhone 17
criticsTake: Critics call the iPhone 17 the best base iPhone in years and the model most people should buy. The 120Hz always-on display, 256GB of base storage at an unchanged $799 price, the Center Stage selfie camera and long battery life drew wide praise. Reviewers still point to the missing telephoto lens, a design that looks like the iPhone 16, USB 2.0 data speeds and heat under heavy load.

name: iPhone 17 Pro
criticsTake: Critics praise the iPhone 17 Pro for its long battery life, its versatile triple 48MP cameras with a sharper 4x telephoto, and a vapor chamber that keeps the A19 Pro cooler under load. The aluminum unibody and wide camera plateau split opinion, and several reviewers note it is heavier than before. The Verge, Ars Technica, PCMag and Tech Advisor all say the cheaper iPhone 17, which shares its 120Hz screen, is the better buy for most people.

name: iPhone Air
criticsTake: Critics agree the design is the iPhone Air's main strength: at 5.64 mm and 165 g it is easy to hold for long periods, and its titanium frame held up in reviewers' drop and bend tests. The cost is a single rear camera, a mono speaker, slower charging and battery life that trails the rest of the iPhone 17 lineup. Most reviewers say it suits people who value thinness above all, and that the cheaper iPhone 17 or the 17 Pro is the better buy for everyone else.

name: Galaxy S26 Ultra
criticsTake: Critics call the Galaxy S26 Ultra a modest update, yet most still rank it among the best Android phones you can buy. The new Privacy Display, which hides the screen from people nearby, draws near-universal praise, along with faster charging, top performance and a slimmer, lighter body. The unchanged 5,000mAh battery, missing Qi2 magnets and small camera changes keep it from feeling like a big step up from the S25 Ultra.

name: Google Pixel 11 Pro
criticsTake: Critics call the Pixel 11 Pro a refined but small update to the Pixel 10 Pro. Reviewers praise its compact build, bright display, strong cameras and new software such as Magic Capture and Rambler voice typing. Most also fault the $100 higher US starting price, less RAM on the base model, weak gaming performance, middling battery life and the HiLight notification light, so Tom's Guide and Android Central suggest the Pixel 10 Pro may be the better buy.
